Possible causes: Operating changes, transient disturbances, instrument issues or developing equipment problems. Recommended checks: Compare vibration (mm/s), machine temperature (\u00b0F), motor load (%), and factory air temperature (\u00b0F) over the same relevant time window. Record ticks, sample counts, minimum and maximum, and a trend, not only the last reading. Separate running from idle periods. Link alarms to the underlying sensor readings and independent evidence. How to interpret: The default line vibration alarm is triggered by a reading above 4.5 mm/s. It is a monitoring setpoint, not a confirmed failure threshold. Missing samples are unknown, never zero. A sensor reading and a maintenance note are evidence; neither is a diagnosis. Observable channels and records: vibration (mm/s per station; speed, load and instruments affect readings); temperature (\u00b0F per station; thermal lag, compare factory air); load (% per station; active machining against idle matters); air temperature (\u00b0F, factory-wide; door and daily variation); power (kW per station; cutting load and speed, plus friction or a straining drive); following error (\u00b5m per station, the feed axis's lag behind its commanded path; \u00a72.14); hydraulic pressure (bar, only on stations fitted with hydraulics; \u00a72.15); events and job history (alarms, job movement, stops; events record observations, not causes); inspections (job, batch, pass or fail; outcomes are statistical); settings and maintenance (the current speed only, and service notes; service history is not present health).", "title": "Measurements, Trends, Alarms and Evidence Quality"}, {"document": "SIM-CNC-001 rev 1.3", "section": "\u00a72.1", "text": "When to consult: One high vibration alarm; recurring peaks; a sustained increase in mm/s during production. Possible causes: Heavier workpiece load, speed change, spindle-bearing deterioration, imbalance, loose mounting, alignment, cutting chatter, or sensor disturbance. Recommended checks: Check whether the machine was running. Compare several consecutive readings and trend windows at similar loads and spindle speeds; look for changes in temperature or load. Check nearby stations for shared effects. Review operating events, setting changes, and prior maintenance. Request a physical inspection when telemetry does not separate mechanical vibration from sensor movement. How to interpret: A single spike without corroboration does not justify a repair. A persistent change across independent signals merits deeper investigation. Do not diagnose a bearing by vibration alone. Possible causes: Shaft or coupling misalignment, imbalanced workholding, loose foundation or mounting hardware, excessive runout, damaged tooling. Recommended checks: Compare vibration at comparable motor loads and speed settings. Review whether behaviour began after maintenance, tool changes or workholding adjustments. If a technician is available, check alignment, runout, fastener condition and rotating balance with suitable instruments while following lockout procedures. How to interpret: A scalar vibration trend cannot identify frequency bands, harmonics, direction or runout. what to find out first
Get CNC-05 raw vibration readings from tick 816 to 830 to verify the alarm context: sample count, per-tick values, min/max, and trend around the 4.56 mm/s reading at tick 826.
I need to know all machines on the line to check whether high vibration is isolated to CNC-05 or seen factory-wide (Q3), and to get each machine's status and current job (relevant to Q4).

Determine whether the CNC-05 vibration spikes are isolated to that machine or seen factory-wide, which separates an isolated developing fault from a factory-wide disturbance; then gather CNC-05's other sensors (temperature, load, power, following error) and event history over the same window.

Whether CNC-05's above-threshold vibration coincides with elevated motor load (supporting an operating/drive cause H4/H1) or occurs at normal load (pointing to a transient/instrument cause H3). CNC-01 peer vibration over the same window is far below the 4.50 mm/s threshold (E5), which weakens a factory-wide disturbance H2 but does not eliminate it. CNC-05's own vibration spikes above threshold only at ticks 826 and 828 and returns to ~4.1-4.4 between (E3), so the cause on CNC-05 is still undetermined; CNC-05 load/temperature/power/following-error and event history (Q2/Q4) and factory air temperature (Q5) remain needed.

CNC-05 temperature over ticks 816-830 to check whether a thermal condition accompanies the vibration spikes at 826 and 828. After this, power and following_error (rest of Q2_rest), CNC-05 event/job history (Q4), and factory air temperature (Q5) remain needed to distinguish H1/H3/H4 and rule out H2.

CNC-05 power (kW) over ticks 816-830 to check whether drive electrical demand is elevated at vibration spike ticks 826/828. Temperature (E7) was relatively flat at spike ticks (147.50°F at 826, 147.96°F at 828 vs. max 148.19°F at 827), so power is the remaining key discriminator between H1/H4 (elevated power at spikes) and H3 (flat power, transient alarm).

CNC-05 following_error over ticks 816-830 to check whether axis lag is elevated at vibration spike ticks 826/828 — the last remaining machine-level discriminator after power (E8), load (E6), and temperature (E7) all proved flat at spike ticks.

Whether CNC-05's event log around ticks 826-828 shows job changes, stops, or other alarms tying the vibration spikes to an operating condition (H4), versus no events supporting a transient/spurious alarm (H3). Power, load, temperature, and following error show no consistent elevation at both spike ticks, so event history is the remaining machine-level discriminator.

Check CNC-02 vibration for ticks 816-830 to see whether it also spikes at ticks 826/828; if CNC-02 is quiet while CNC-05 spikes, the factory-wide disturbance hypothesis (H2) is further ruled out and the transient CNC-05-only alarm (H3) gains support. CNC-01 is already known quiet (E5), so CNC-02/03/04 are the remaining unchecked machines for a complete factory scan.

Whether CNC-03 (then CNC-04) also vibrates above ~4.5 mm/s at ticks 826/828. If neither does, H2 (factory-wide disturbance) is ruled out and H3 (transient CNC-05-only alarm) becomes the leading explanation. Still open afterward: Q4 spindle-speed comparison across machines and Q5 factory air temperature.
Whether CNC-04 (the last unchecked machine) also vibrates above ~4.5 mm/s at ticks 826/828, completing the factory-wide scan to rule out H2; Q4 spindle-speed comparison remains open afterward.

Whether CNC-05's spindle speed setting differs from the other machines (Q4_residual) — the last open question that separates H3 from H4. H2 is already excluded by the completed factory vibration scan (all other machines stay well under 4.50 mm/s at ticks 826/828), and H1 is contradicted by flat power/load/temperature at the spike ticks (E6-E9).

Whether CNC-05 vibration persists above the 4.50 mm/s threshold or worsens after tick 830 — the one check that could still shift the conclusion between a developing fault (H1, expects persistence/worsening with concurrent power/load/following_error elevation) and a transient spurious alarm (H3, expects return to ~4.1-4.47 with flat concurrent sensors). E8 already shows power is flat at spike ticks (12.452 kW at 826, 12.449 kW at 828, within 12.2-12.7 kW range), so Q2_power is answered; E14 already gives per-machine standard speeds (CNC-05 1100 rpm is its own normal setting), so the H4 speed check is answered; Q5 separates no hypotheses and other machines' normal vibration (E11-E13) already rules out a factory-wide disturbance. Only vibration persistence after tick 830 remains untested.

Whether CNC-05 vibration persists above 4.50 mm/s after tick 830 — the pending discriminating check between H1 (developing fault expects persistence/worsening) and H3 (transient alarm expects return to ~4.1-4.47). Q2_power is already answered by E8 (power flat at spike ticks: 12.452 kW at 826, 12.449 kW at 828, within 12.2-12.7 kW). Q5 separates no hypotheses and is not decision-relevant. E15 only advanced time to tick 840; no post-830 vibration reading exists yet.

Whether CNC-05 power is elevated after tick 830 while vibration stays high — the key discriminator between H1 (developing mechanical fault draws more power) and H3 (transient/spurious alarm with normal power).

The evidence is sufficient to diagnose the CNC-05 vibration alarm. Q2_power and Q_power_post830 are both answered: CNC-05 power was flat during 816-830 (E8: min 12.2075, max 12.7071, mean 12.468 kW, no elevation at spike ticks 826/828) and flat during 830-840 (E17: min 12.2027, max 12.882, mean 12.4894 kW). H1's prediction (a developing mechanical fault draws more power concurrent with sustained vibration) fails, so H1 is effectively ruled out. H3's prediction (flat power/load/temperature/following_error with transient threshold crossings) holds: load (E6), temperature (E7), following_error (E9) were all flat across 816-830, and no job/stop/speed-change events occurred at 826/828 (E10), contradicting H4. H2 is contradicted by normal vibration on CNC-01..CNC-04 (E5, E11, E12, E13; all ≤2.50 mm/s vs CNC-05's 3.83-4.57 mm/s). CNC-05 vibration remains elevated (E16: 4.06-4.53 mm/s post-830) even though the alarm crossings were transient, so an elevated baseline on CNC-05 is a real observation worth flagging, but no fault signature supports a repair call. Q5 (factory air temperature around 826) remains unanswered but is indirect, separates no hypotheses, and cannot change the diagnosis given all other machines are normal; spending a call on it is not justified. One discriminating check (power post-830) was already completed via E17 and supports H3.
what could explain the evidence

Q2_power and Q_power_post830 are already answered by E8 and E17: CNC-05 power is flat (~12.45-12.49 kW) at vibration spike ticks 826/828 and over ticks 830-840, with no elevation—no mechanical-fault power signature. The remaining discriminating need is T1/T3: was CNC-05's ~4.3 mm/s vibration already elevated before tick 816 / before job 9 started at tick 802, or did it step up recently? A pre-816 vibration window for CNC-05 separates long-standing baseline (H1/H3) from a recent step change (possible new fault or job-linked H3).

the diagnosis and what to do about it

conclusion.diagnosis: CNC-05 shows persistently elevated vibration (~4.0-4.5 mm/s) with isolated threshold crossings at ticks 826 and 828 (4.56 and 4.57 mm/s above the 4.50 mm/s alarm threshold). All other CNC-05 sensors are flat and normal: power was ~12.45 kW at both alarm ticks (well within the 12.2-12.7 kW normal range), load mean 68.96%, temperature mean 147.19 °F, following_error mean 4.96 µm with no spike. CNC-05's vibration is roughly double the other CNC machines (CNC-01 mean 1.00, CNC-02 mean 2.06, CNC-03 mean 1.05, CNC-04 mean 1.80 mm/s). The elevated vibration predates job 9 (ticks 800-816 mean 4.04 mm/s), so it is not job-specific. No mechanical fault is indicated: there is no power draw increase, load increase, temperature rise, or following_error growth at or after the alarm ticks. The most consistent explanations are H2 (vibration sensor calibration drift/bias reading ~2 mm/s high) or H3 (CNC-05's normal operating band with a fixed 4.50 mm/s threshold that is too low for this machine). Neither H2 nor H3 can be confirmed over the other with current data, and neither is addressable by the available repair actions (replace_bearing, reset_setting, replace_servo_drive, repair_hydraulics).
unresolved_questions: Whether CNC-05's elevated vibration is caused by sensor calibration drift (H2) or is a genuine machine-specific operating band with an inappropriately low alarm threshold (H3).
CNC-05 power (kW) over ticks 816-830 — is it elevated at vibration spike ticks 826/828?
Is CNC-05 power (kW) elevated over ticks 830-840 while vibration remains ~4.06-4.53 mm/s? Distinguishes H1 (mechanical fault draws more power) from H3 (normal power, transient alarm).
Does an independent reference vibration measurement at CNC-05 agree with the machine's channel (~4.3 mm/s), or does it read about 2 mm/s lower, indicating channel bias?
Was CNC-05's vibration already ~4.3 mm/s before job 9 started at tick 802, or did it step up when job 9 began?
conclusion.next_check: Take an independent reference vibration measurement at CNC-05 (portable sensor or maintenance inspection) and compare against the machine's channel (~4.3 mm/s); if the independent reading is ~1-2.5 mm/s, H2 is confirmed (sensor bias); if it also reads ~4.3 mm/s, H3 is confirmed (normal band, threshold too low).

critique.favoured_claim: Transient/spurious alarm: brief threshold crossings at ticks 826 and 828 on a stable, elevated CNC-05 vibration baseline (~4.3 mm/s); no underlying physical fault, with power, load, temperature, and following_error all flat.
critique.why: H1 (transient/spurious alarm) is the best fit because it explains the isolated vibration threshold crossings at ticks 826 and 828 (E10) while accounting for the stable baseline (~4.3 mm/s) observed in E3, E16, and E18. Other sensors (power, load, temperature, following_error) remain flat (E6, E7, E8, E9, E17), and no upward trend or new fault signatures appear post-alarm. H2 (sensor calibration drift) is less likely because the vibration readings are consistent with a stable elevated baseline rather than a persistent ~2 mm/s bias across all samples, and other machines (E5, E11, E12, E13) show no similar bias. H3 (normal operating condition) is contradicted by E12, where CNC-03's vibration is far lower despite similar speed settings (E14), and the alarm threshold is fixed, not machine-specific.
critique.discriminating_check: get_sensor_trend for CNC-05 vibration from tick 840 to 900 (bucket_ticks=60) to confirm whether the vibration remains stable (~4.3 mm/s) or trends upward, which would refute H1 and support H2 or C2.

objections.text: H3 (normal operating condition) could still apply if CNC-05's vibration is consistently higher due to job-specific factors, but E12 (CNC-03's vibration) contradicts this by showing lower values at a higher speed (1200 rpm vs. CNC-05's 1100 rpm).
No independent vibration measurement (e.g., portable sensor) was taken to confirm whether the elevated readings are due to sensor bias (H2) or true vibration (H1/H3).
H2 assumes the bias is confined to the vibration sensor, but no evidence rules out other sensors being similarly affected.

recheck.question: The critic's check: get_sensor_trend for CNC-05 vibration from tick 840 to 900 (bucket_ticks=60) to confirm whether the vibration remains stable (~4.3 mm/s) or trends upward, which would refute H1 and support H2 or C2.

RUN-01.name: evidence_quality
RUN-01.instructions: Read `trace`. Judge whether the final `conclusion.diagnosis` is supported by relevant evidence the factory itself returned (origin 'observable'), rather than by assumptions, manual guidance or memory alone. Consider only evidence ids the conclusion or the selected hypothesis cites and what those items actually contain.
criteria: 0: The conclusion cites no observable evidence, or the cited evidence does not bear on the claim.
1: One cited observable item loosely relates to the claim; key symptoms the claim depends on were never read.
2: Cited observable evidence shows the symptom the claim names, but a plausible alternative explanation of the same evidence was not examined.
3: Cited observable evidence shows the symptom and at least one discriminating reading was made that separates the claim from an alternative.
4: Cited observable evidence shows the symptom, discriminating readings separate it from the alternatives, and other machines or batches were checked before the conclusion.
RUN-01.missing_evidence: If trace.completeness is record_only, do not ask; record unknown.
RUN-01.deterministic_precedence: evaluator_only.evidence_share and relevant_evidence_collected give the truth-side view of coverage; this question gives the judge's view of whether what was collected supports what was concluded. Report both, never one for the other.
RUN-01.scoring_note: Report the probability-weighted score and the modal level; a mean below 2 on a run scored root_cause_correct=true is flagged 'misleading success'.

RUN-02.name: hypothesis_reasoning
RUN-02.instructions: Read `trace.hypotheses`, `trace.pruned_candidates` and the decisions in phase 'test'. Judge whether the investigator considered competing plausible causes for the anomaly and tested them against each other, rather than pursuing one explanation from the start.
criteria: 0: One hypothesis only, or several hypotheses that are rewordings of the same cause.
1: Several distinct hypotheses were listed but no decision in the test phase was aimed at telling them apart.
2: Distinct hypotheses and at least one test-phase reading that bears on a rival, but confidences moved without the cited evidence changing.
3: Distinct hypotheses, discriminating readings, and confidences revised in a way the cited evidence explains.
4: As 3, and a hypothesis that needs no change to the factory (a transient, a batch, a setting) was held and tested, not only mechanical faults.

RUN-03.name: critic_effectiveness
RUN-03.instructions: Read `trace.critique`, `trace.recheck`, the hypotheses and the conclusion. Did the critic identify an important weakness (a contradiction, a missing check, a better alternative) and did a useful follow-up happen when one was warranted?

criteria.effective: The critic named a real weakness or the best-supported alternative, and the follow-up reading (or the conclusion) reflects it.
criteria.ineffective: The critic missed an evident weakness, objected without substance, or its point was available and ignored (recheck skipped, policy_stopped, or the conclusion unchanged despite a contradicting reading).
criteria.not_required: The leading hypothesis was already well supported and the critic's agreement was reasonable; no follow-up was needed.
criteria.unknown: No usable critique (outcome no_answer or invalid_reply), or the trace is incomplete.

RUN-03.missing_evidence: No critique record: not asked; recorded as not_run.
RUN-03.applies_to: one master-run packet with trace.critique present
RUN-03.deterministic_precedence: critique.verdict_mismatch, recheck.outcome and recheck.trigger are code facts; evaluator_only.critic_pick_correct says whether the pick named the true cause. Those are reported beside this answer.

RUN-04.name: retrieval_quality
RUN-04.instructions: Read `trace.manual_searches`, `trace.recall_searches`, the evidence items whose origin is 'manual' or 'memory', and where those ids are cited. Did the retrieved passages or memories materially support the investigation?

criteria.useful: A retrieved section or memory is cited by a hypothesis, a decision or the conclusion, and the reasoning that cites it is consistent with its content.
criteria.unnecessary: Retrieval happened but nothing retrieved was cited or acted on; the investigation would read the same without it.
criteria.misleading: A retrieved item was cited in support of a claim it does not support, or steered a reading away from the symptom.
criteria.not_retrieved: The tool was offered but never answered a search (no search, or every search refused or failed).

RUN-04.missing_evidence: Neither offered: not asked; recorded as not_offered.
RUN-04.applies_to: one master-run packet with manual or memory offered
RUN-04.deterministic_precedence: search counts, refusals and the sections returned are code facts (manual_searches, recall_searches); whether a memory was cited is `memory_uses.used` in the record.

RUN-05.name: verification_demonstrated
RUN-05.instructions: Read `trace.verification`, `trace.proposal` and the evidence observed after `action_finish_tick` (or after the conclusion for a no-action run). Does the trace show that the agent checked its prediction against observations made after the work, and that the verdict follows from them?

criteria.yes: Observable evidence with a data window after the work (or after the conclusion) was read, the verdict cites it, and the cited values agree with the verdict.
criteria.no: No look after the work, the verdict cites evidence from before the work, or the cited values contradict the verdict.
criteria.not_applicable: The run ended with escalate or without a proposal, so no remedy was there to verify.

RUN-05.deterministic_precedence: The loop already refuses a verdict that rests on evidence from before the work (`capstone.agent.investigation.verify`); evaluator_only.verification_calibration compares the verdict with the truth. This question adds only whether the cited numbers support the verdict.

RUN-06.name: abstention_appropriate
RUN-06.instructions: Read the conclusion, its confidence and assessment, and the evidence. If the agent declined to name a cause (escalate / unresolved) was the evidence in fact insufficient? If it named a cause with high confidence, was the evidence sufficient for that confidence?

criteria.appropriate: Declined when the evidence left two or more causes open, or committed when the cited evidence settles the cause.
criteria.inappropriate: Declined although the cited evidence settled the cause, or committed with confidence 0.8 or more while a rival cause was untested or a contradiction stood.
criteria.not_applicable: The run never reached a reasoned conclusion (model unavailable, undetermined by timeout).

RUN-06.deterministic_precedence: evaluator_only.abstained and confident_wrong are code facts from the label and the truth; this question judges the decision against the evidence shown, not against the truth.

RUN-07.name: failure_classification
RUN-07.instructions: Read the whole trace. What most seriously undermined this investigation? Choose the single earliest cause that, had it gone right, would most likely have changed the outcome.

criteria.reasoning: The relevant readings were in hand and misread: the hypotheses or confidences do not follow from the cited evidence.
criteria.retrieval: A manual or memory answer was absent, unhelpful or misleading at the point it mattered.
criteria.critic: The critic missed or misdirected, or its correct point was dropped.
criteria.tooling: Tool errors, refused calls, repeated calls, a blackout or a gap left the needed reading unavailable, or the budget ran out before it could be made.
criteria.verification: The diagnosis and action were right but the post-action check was missing or wrong.
criteria.none_observed: Nothing undermined it: the investigation reads as sound.

RUN-07.missing_evidence: record_only packets: the judge may use tools_used, decisions outcomes and termination_reason only; answer unknown unless a tooling or timeout cause is evident from them.
RUN-07.applies_to: one master-run packet; asked of every run, with none_observed for one that reads as sound, so the judge never learns from the question which runs were wrong
RUN-07.deterministic_precedence: evaluator_only.miss_kind (evidence_miss vs reasoning_miss) and facts.termination_reason are code facts reported beside this answer.

RUN-08.name: conclusion_support
RUN-08.instructions: Independently of whether the diagnosis is true, how well does the trace support the final conclusion as stated? Consider the cited evidence, the unexplained and contradicting evidence the hypotheses list, open questions, and whether the stated confidence matches.
criteria: 0: The conclusion is not supported: cited evidence is absent, irrelevant or contradicts it.
1: Weakly supported: one consistent reading, with alternatives or contradictions left open.
2: Partly supported: the symptom is shown, but at least one listed contradiction, unexplained item or open question remains.
3: Well supported: the cited evidence shows the symptom and separates the cause from the alternatives the agent considered.
4: Fully supported: as 3, with the confidence stated proportionate and nothing material left open.
RUN-08.deterministic_precedence: `check_conclusion` already lowers an unresolved conclusion to escalate; this question measures the quality of the text and citations, which code cannot.

RUN-11.name: critic_feedback_used
RUN-11.instructions: Read `trace.critique` (the check it named), `trace.recheck` and the hypotheses before and after. Did the investigator use the critic's feedback?

criteria.used: The follow-up reading was made where the critic pointed, and the leading hypothesis or its confidence changed in the direction the reading supports (or stayed when the reading confirmed it).
criteria.ignored: A usable critique named a check and the follow-up was skipped, stopped by the policy, refused, or made but the beliefs did not respond to what it showed.
criteria.no_feedback: The critic gave no usable check (no_answer, invalid_reply, or an empty discriminating_check).

RUN-11.missing_evidence: No recheck record: not asked (the follow-up was off).
RUN-11.applies_to: one master-run packet with trace.critique and trace.recheck present
RUN-11.deterministic_precedence: recheck.outcome, confidence_before and confidence_after are code facts; this question adds whether the response to the reading was sensible.

RUN-12.name: evidence_cited_matches_content
RUN-12.instructions: For each evidence id the conclusion cites, read that item's content. Does every cited item actually show what the conclusion says it shows?

criteria.true: Every cited item contains the reading, event or result the conclusion attributes to it.
criteria.false: At least one cited item does not contain what is attributed to it (wrong machine, wrong sensor, a value not present, an event not there), or the conclusion cites nothing.

RUN-12.deterministic_precedence: `check_conclusion` verifies that cited ids exist and `verify_numeric_claims` checks structured numbers; neither checks the prose. This question covers the prose.
